texto: It was a busy evening with a smooth service. The PDR group had an excellent experience and gave a round of applause for Claudio, who was outstanding. Please note, the main entrance door to Penny Blue is currently broken and requires maintenance.
It was an overall busy evening at Exchange Lane.
We got busy around 9:30 pm and had a group of 15 guests join us.

Guests on Table 24 were disappointed with the food. They said the steak was bland and not done to their liking and chips were stale. Chefs offered to make a new steak and give desserts but the guests refused. They ate the entire meal and we took the steak off their cheque. They were happy that we took it off the cheque.

Table 34 raised concerns regarding the difference between the advertised 425ml pour for tap beers on our menu and the 350ml glasses provided instead. To resolve the issue, a complimentary round of beers was offered. Additionally, they noted that the steak and mash was served cold.

It was a busy evening in Penny Blue. We had 18 pre ordered beef wellingtons and sold 2 more additionally. We sold a few good wines such as Charles Heidsick Champagne, Pol Roger Brut Reserve and Tolpuddle Pinot Noir. It was a smooth evening overall.

Room 624 was dining in Exchange Lane, kitchen missed sending their fries and forgot to add avacado to their grain salad. We took the chicken skewers and fries off the check. Guests were fine when they left, morning team has been informed to take special care.
Guests from the ATAC event arrived at the bar around 4:30 PM, resulting in a busy period, followed by an additional inflow of guests after the football game  at 10:00 PM.
Room 1306 order a gluten free bolognese, however, there was an oversight which led to a one hour delay. The guest was understanding and as a part of service recovery we took it off the cheque.

Table 41, our regular guests, ordered a well done steak but recieved a medium steak instead. The kitchen offered to remake it, however the guest denied. As a part of service recovery, we gave them a complimentary dessert.
Room 922, rejected their amenity (Lashes pacific ale)  since they weren't keen on drinking alchol. The Manager on duty gave them a drinks voucher for the bar instead.

The guests ordered a bottle of Pommery Champagne and a serve of natural oysters. Subsequently, the chef informed that oysters were unavailable. As the guests were particularly keen on having oysters, complimentary warm olives and fries were offered as a gesture of service recovery. The guests were appreciative of the gesture and departed satisfied.
Two rooms placed orders using incorrect room numbers tonight which resulted in a delay. Once the room numbers were corrected, the orders were delivered promptly.
Room 1422 ordered some of our most expensive wines such as  Winston Churchill Champagne, Hill of grace and Penfolds Grange.

Table 7: Pita bread & dips ordered at 15:15 were delayed 30+ mins due to no chef present. Guest requested and received a full refund with an apology.
Table 2: Order placed at 19:30 took 35 mins to prepare. Guest was visibly unhappy but declined complimentary drinks. Beverage charges were removed as a service recovery, and the guest was satisfied.

Room 922 – Mr. & Mrs. Smith – Breakfast
Mr. and Mrs. Smith arrived at Penny Blue during a busy breakfast service when the restaurant was at full capacity. They were informed of an estimated waiting time of 10–15 minutes.
The guests advised they would instead have breakfast at the M Club. As a gesture, their usual coffee order was offered before they headed upstairs, which they were happy to accept.
While the host desk was attending to other arriving guests, other waiting guests were seated before Mr. and Mrs. Smith were offered a table. Their coffee order was also delayed by more than 15 minutes, so they proceeded to the M Club for breakfast.
The coffee was personally delivered to the M Club, and the guests were also offered their preferred egg order with sourdough from Penny Blue, which they politely declined. The guests expressed disappointment with the delay in receiving their coffee and the wait for a table.
Later that day, Thisuri personally met with the couple at Exchange Lane, apologized for their breakfast experience, and arranged a service recovery. Ms. Regina was offered a complimentary French Martini, and a bottle of Sauvignon Blanc, a cheesecake, and a handwritten apology card were sent to the room for the couple.

Exchange Lane had a steady flow of guests throughout the day, with the majority being in-house guests dining with us for food. While the venue was not particularly busy, there was a consistent level of business, allowing the team to provide attentive and efficient service. Service ran smoothly throughout the shift, and all guests were happy with their dining experience.

In-Room Dining had a consistent flow of orders throughout the evening. The busiest period was between 6:00 pm and 8:00 pm, during which the team experienced the highest volume of orders. Service was managed efficiently, and orders were delivered in a timely manner.

We hosted two groups in the restaurant tonight: Emirates and Electrolux, with 12 guests in each group. We also welcomed a group of 23 guests from APT Travel in the Private Dining Room. All services ran smoothly, and guests were happy with their dining experience.
The bar got busy between 5:30PM to 6:00 PM today.
The bar got extremely busy between 18:00 - 21:30 PM, with several small groups joining us. We majorly had inhouse guests coming in for food. Service ran smoothly and all guests left satisfied.
IRD got busy at the same time as the bar. We had slight delays on orders but guests were updated about the expected waiting periods.

We hosted a group of 23 guests from APT Travel in the Private Dining Room. The group has a series of contracted dinners with us and thoroughly enjoyed both the food and service. The evening was well received, with positive feedback from the guests throughout the dinner.

The APT Travel group joined us in the bar from 5:45 PM for pre-dinner drinks before heading to Penny Blue for dinner. The bar had a steady flow of guests throughout the evening, with consistent activity until around 10:00 PM.

It was a busy evening in Penny Blue. We hosted a group of 13 guests in the PDR, who ordered nearly 50 cocktails throughout the night. The group thoroughly enjoyed the food and service, with a total spend of approximately $3,500.

This evening, we ran a new soup special — cream of chorizo and cauliflower, topped with chilli oil. The Angus O’Connor T-bone also continued as a special and was very well received throughout the week.

We also introduced five new wines as part of our Sommelier’s Pick selection this week.

Table 1: Guest advised that the linguine was extremely spicy. A crème brûlée was offered as a service recovery gesture.

C1: Guest advised that the baby squid was not to their liking. The item was removed from the bill.

Guest in room 1214 ordered room service; however, due to a technical error, the order was delivered to room 1124. The guest contacted AYS and was understandably upset. An attempt was made to contact the guest to apologise, but there was no response. An amenity will be sent tomorrow as a service recovery gesture.
Penny Blue picked up a few walk-ins throughout the evening. We also had a very strong night for bottled wine sales. Overall, guests were very happy with the service and their experience.

Exchange Lane had a steady flow of guests throughout the night. We welcomed the Elders Group for pre-dinner drinks. There was a slight delay with food orders during service while the kitchen was busy managing a high volume of IRD orders
Please note that figures in the report may be inaccurate, as the Infrasys system was down from 11:00 PM until 12:30 AM.

We ran the new Angus O’Connor T-Bone special, served with Diane sauce, selling 10 serves across last night and tonight. The special was very well received, with great feedback from guests. We also sold 9 Beef Wellingtons tonight.

It was a busy night with smooth service throughout and everything running well.

Mr. and Mrs. Miner from Room 1122 had a reservation at Penny Blue but did not dine with us.

Penny Blue remained very busy throughout the evening, with a consistent flow of guests until the end of service. We also picked up a strong number of walk-ins throughout the evening. A group of 21 guests from APT Travel dined in the Private Dining Room. Overall, guests enjoyed the food and drinks, with positive feedback received throughout the evening.
The bar was relatively quiet between 7:00 pm and 9:00 pm. It then became busy from 9:00 pm until approximately 11:30 pm.

A group of 33 guests dined in the Private Dining Room to celebrate a regular guest's friend's 50th birthday. The evening commenced with 45 minutes of pre-dinner drinks in the Great Room, followed by dinner in the Private Dining Room. The guests enjoyed a selection of cocktails and bottled wines throughout the evening and provided positive feedback on the food, beverages, and service. Overall, the function was a great success, and the guests had an enjoyable experience.

In-house guests from Room 804 dined with us and thoroughly enjoyed their meal, particularly the Confit Duck Leg. At the conclusion of service, they provided feedback that the cheesecake was dry. As a service recovery gesture, the dessert was removed from the bill. The guests were appreciative of the resolution and left satisfied, complimenting both the food and overall service.

Exchange Lane experienced a busy period between 4:00 PM and 8:00 PM, with it picking up again around 10:00 PM. We welcomed a large number of in-house guests dining throughout the evening. Service ran smoothly.
IRD got busy between 17:30PM and 19:30PM.

Exchange Lane was busy throughout the evening with a steady flow of guests, primarily in-house guests visiting for drinks.

Guests from Room 1122 dined in Exchange Lane and ordered an Exchange Lane Club Sandwich and a Kids' Fish & Chips. Due to a miscommunication when the order was taken, only the club sandwich was entered into the system. At the time, the kitchen was experiencing a high volume of in-room dining orders, resulting in approximately a 30-minute wait for the club sandwich. Once the meal was served, it was identified that the Kids' Fish & Chips had not been entered. The order was immediately prioritised by the kitchen, and the guests were informed of the error and updated on the expected wait time. Although the meal was prepared within approximately 10 minutes, the guests had already returned to their room. As a gesture of goodwill, the Kids' Fish & Chips was delivered to the room with complimentary ice cream for the child and parent, and the fish & chips was removed from the bill. The guests appreciated the apology and recovery gesture and were satisfied with the resolution.

In-Room Dining experienced a high volume of orders between 6:00 pm and 9:00 pm, with a constant flow of orders. Due to the demand across both In-Room Dining and the bar, guests were advised of wait times of up to 45 minutes. Despite the high volume, all orders were delivered within the advised timeframe.

A guest in Room 1310 ordered a Caesar Salad with chicken and an additional poached egg. Due to an order mix-up, the salad was initially delivered without the additional items. The error was identified shortly after delivery, and the guest was contacted immediately. The chicken was delivered promptly, followed by the additional poached egg once it was confirmed that the guest had requested an extra egg in addition to the standard poached egg included with the dish. As a gesture of goodwill, a complimentary glass of Chardonnay was provided. Approximately one hour later, the guest advised Front Office that they were dissatisfied with the meal, stating it lacked flavour and had been delivered without salt and pepper. Attempts to contact the guest by both the outlet and the MOD were unsuccessful. The Caesar Salad was removed from the guest's account, and the MOD will follow up with the guest the following morning to apologise and confirm the charge has been waived.
Exchange Lane experienced a slow evening service, with the majority of guests being in-house patrons enjoying beverages. Food orders were minimal, and service ran smoothly throughout the shift.
In-Room Dining became busy from approximately 9:30 PM due to a high volume of Emirates crew orders. Service was well managed, and all orders were delivered in a timely manner.

It was a busy evening at Penny Blue, with a high volume of in-house guests dining throughout the service. The team worked efficiently, ensuring a smooth service and a positive dining experience for all guests. Beverage sales were strong, with excellent bottle wine sales including Hentley Farm Clos Otto, La Chablisienne Premier Cru, and several other premium selections. Cocktail sales were also particularly strong, with the Mushroom Manhattan proving to be a guest favourite. One guest enjoyed the cocktail so much that they ordered it three times during their visit. Overall, the service ran seamlessly, and guests were highly satisfied with their dining experience.

A guest from Room 410 dined at Exchange Lane and ordered the Prawn Linguine. After tasting the dish, the guest advised that they felt something was not quite right with it. The kitchen promptly inspected the dish and confirmed that it had been prepared correctly and was in line with the recipe specification. As a service recovery gesture, the team offered to replace the meal with an alternative dish from the menu, which the guest selected and was served promptly.

A Titanium Elite guest in Room 820 placed an in-room dining order via the QR code for the Steamed Greens and Gochujang Chicken, which was prepared and delivered as ordered. Shortly after delivery, the guest placed a second order via the QR code for the Bolognese. Upon delivery of the second order, the guest returned the first meal untouched, stating that the incorrect order had initially been delivered. A review of the order history confirmed that both orders had been placed by the guest through the QR ordering system, with the first order accurately prepared and delivered as requested. As a service recovery gesture, the Bolognese was provided to the guest, while the initial meal remained untouched and was discarded. The incident appeared to have resulted from confusion with the QR ordering system rather than an error in order preparation or delivery.

It was a busy evening at Penny Blue, with a high volume of in-house guests dining throughout the service. Big table of 8 order plenty wines we sold Tolpuddle Chardonnay E.Guigal Gigondas Grenache,  and several other premium selections along with a lot of house reds and whites were sold by the bottle namely the Bin 28 and the Pol Roger Brut reserve Champange

Exchange Lane was steady through the night. After light was busy with heavy spending tables which carried on into the night. The event upstair finished and the major crowd headed downstairs for a nightcap.

Room 1005 waited for around 45 minutes for a soup and a few drinks but the guest was taken care of the staff and service recovery was provided and the guest was extremly happy and appreciated the gesture shown.

The APT group dinner was held in the PDR tonight. The group began with pre-dinner drinks at Exchange Lane before moving to Penny Blue at 6:30 PM.

The event flowed smoothly, and the guests enjoyed both the food and service.

The APT group arrived at Exchange Lane at 18:00 for pre-dinner drinks. The busiest period of the evening service was between 18:00 and 20:00, with several in-house guests also joining us for dinner.

There were some delays with food orders, as the kitchen was managing multiple orders across all outlets, including Penny Blue entrées, In-Room Dining, and Exchange Lane. Guests were informed of the expected wait times and were understanding of the situation.

Room 914 ordered a Marriott Burger and brownie through In-Room Dining at 21:15. The guest later contacted At Your Service to report finding a piece of plastic in the food and advised that she did not wish to continue eating.

The Assistant Restaurant Manager visited the room to check on the guest and offered further assistance; however, the guest declined any replacement food or additional items. The entire food order was removed from the bill. As a service recovery gesture, a complimentary beverage voucher and an apology letter were delivered and placed outside the guest’s room.

Guest on table 41 had ordered the magra Lamb shoulder and found a rubber band and hair in it and informed the serve during clearance  and the lamb was taken off from the bill and the guest was happy with that and didnt have any issues while leaving.
Bar sold many high end spirits tonight includimg the Louis 13 cognac
IRD went smoothly orders went on time and there were no issues or delays in order

It was a very busy evening, with a high volume of guests throughout the restaurant. Service flowed smoothly, and guests were happy and satisfied with their overall dining experience.

The Private Dining Room hosted a 21st birthday celebration for 21 guests. The group had a fantastic evening and thoroughly enjoyed the celebrations. Cocktails were very popular throughout the night, making for a lively atmosphere and strong beverage sales. The event ran seamlessly, and the guests were extremely happy with the service. Additionally, our weekly specials were very well received. The Squid Ink Linguine with Crab Meat was a popular choice for the main course throughout the week, receiving excellent feedback from guests. The Vanilla Panna Cotta with Fresh Berries dessert special was also a favourite and was consistently well received across the week

Room 821 – Mr. Collins (Ambassador Elite) visited Exchange Lane in the evening with a Coffee Card voucher. Upon being advised that the voucher was not valid for alcoholic beverages, the guest visited Front Office and obtained a "Meet Me at the Bar" voucher, which is valid for house beer and house wine. The guest requested a cocktail instead and expressed disappointment with the voucher inclusions. As a service recovery gesture, we offered the guest a complimentary cocktail. The guest was appreciative of the resolution and left satisfied. The MOD was informed of the incident.

At approximately 10:30, the guest in Room 806 placed an order with At Your Service (AYS) for a Marriott Burger. The order was inadvertently not entered into the system by AYS. At approximately 11:30, the guest contacted AYS to follow up on the order. During the call, the AYS associate asked whether the guest would like anything else. The guest replied “no.” Due to a misunderstanding, the associate incorrectly assumed that the guest no longer wished to receive the Marriott Burger, and no further action was taken regarding the original order.

Following the guest’s call at 11:30, the Front Office arranged for an ice cream to be delivered to the guest’s room as a gesture of service recovery.

At approximately 12:30, the guest contacted AYS again to enquire about the outstanding order. The error was identified, and the Kitchen team was immediately notified. The Chef kindly remained on duty to prepare the Marriott Burger, which was delivered to the guest within 15 minutes of the second follow-up call.

As a further gesture of goodwill, the Marriott Burger was removed from the guest’s account and provided complimentary.

We hosted a 10 pax Bupa Executive Dinner. À la carte menu with premium wine selection (Yalumba The Octavius Shiraz & M3 Chardonnay). Food was very well received, and guests had an excellent dining experience.

Exchange Lane hosted the After Light event from 4:00 PM to 7:00 PM, attracting a strong turnout of non-resident guests. The mulled wine was particularly well received due to the cold weather. There was a 20-minute delay in serving the cheese board for Table 204. The guests were dissatisfied with the wait, and as a service recovery, the Assistant F&B Manager waived the charges for the item.

Penny Blue commenced service with 30 reservations and finished the evening with a total of 53 guests, supported by a strong number of walk-in diners. The restaurant experienced a busy period throughout the service, however, operations ran smoothly. Overall, guests appeared satisfied with both the food and service.

A guest in Room 626 ordered a Caesar Salad and requested the dressing on the side. After delivery, the guest contacted Front Office to report that no dressing had been provided and that the salad was also missing the bacon included in the standard menu item.

The kitchen team promptly prepared a replacement Caesar Salad and delivered it to the guest. After receiving the replacement, the guest advised that it had been sent without Parmesan cheese.

The issue was acknowledged, and a sincere apology was extended. As a service recovery measure, the Caesar Salad was removed from the guest’s account and no charge was applied. The guest was also offered an alternative meal but declined any further food items.

Penny Blue experienced a very busy evening service and was fully booekd throughout the night. Despite the high volume of guests, service ran smoothly acorss all areas. Guests thoroughly enjoyed their food and beverages, and the team recieved positive feedback on both the quality of the dining experience and the service provided.
The bar got busy between 18:00 - 20:00 tonight. Everything ran smoothly and the guests were satisfied.

Guests at Table 34 ordered the Beef Wellington and were advised of an estimated wait time of 90 minutes. Due to the kitchen missing the docket, the Wellington was served after approximately 120 minutes. While waiting, the guests ordered the Mariner’s Pie and Prawn Linguine. The guests expressed dissatisfaction with the Prawn Linguine, stating that it was tasteless and overly fishy. A replacement dish was prepared and sent by the chef; however, the guests remained dissatisfied with the flavour. The guests also provided feedback that the Mariner’s Pie was overpriced for the portion size and did not represent good value for money.As part of the service recovery, the Prawn Linguine was removed from the final bill. As the guests were celebrating their wedding anniversary, the chef also prepared a personalised anniversary dessert plate, and both the special Mango Gateaux and Chocolate Tart were provided complimentary. Despite the delay and initial concerns with the meals, the guests were highly impressed with the Beef Wellington and expressed appreciation for the service recovery efforts. The guests departed satisfied with the overall service and dining experience.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    Additionally, guests at Table 12 provided feedback during the meal check that the first bite of the Prawn Cocktail was overly spicy; however, they advised that the remainder of the dish was satisfactory and consumed the entrée in full. Upon receiving their main course, the guests ,mentioned that the chips were not served hot enough. The chips were returned to the kitchen and remade by the chef. As a service recovery gesture, a complimentary Crème Brûlée was presented to the table.The guests later expressed dissatisfaction with the Crème Brûlée, stating that it had been assumed they would enjoy the dessert. When settling their account, the guests requested that the Prawn Cocktail be removed from the bill. The item was removed from the final check as requested.

Exchange Lane Bar experienced increased activity after 9:00 p.m., with two external groups joining the venue for drinks, in addition to an in-house Nexia Group. The bar remained busy throughout the late evening period, however, service was delivered smoothly, and operations ran efficiently.

Room #402 – Jack George came to Exchange Lane for lunch today with two other guests. They ordered a Marriott Burger, Entrée Caesar Salad, Kingfish Poke Bowl, and Gochujang Chicken at 1:57 pm. Unfortunately, the food was delayed for more than 50 minutes. The kitchen prepared everything except the Caesar Salad within around 40 minutes, but the salad needed another 5–10 minutes as the ingredients were not ready to go. We informed the guest about the delay while serving the other items. However, the salad took longer than expected, and the guest came to the counter to follow up. The order was ready shortly after.              Additionally, table 07 – Exchange Lane Club order was delayed by more than 45 minutes after being placed at 2:09 pm.When I spoke to the guest about the delay, she mentioned she needed to leave for a meeting. We arranged the meal as a takeaway and let her know there would be no charge due to the wait.

Room 1115 and 812 experienced a delay of one hour for their room service orders since the kitchen had recieved a high volume of orders between 18:30 to 20:00 PM. As a part of service recovery, we offered the guest a complimentary bottle of shiraz. The guests were informed of the expected delay and were satisfied with the overall experience.

A guest from room 1011 ordered a medium rare eye fillet and was extremely dissapointed since it was not evenly cooked and wasn't upto his liking. The guest barely ate the steak and refused for it to be re made. The chefs confirmed that the steak was cooked appropriately. As a part of service recovery, the steak was taken off the cheque. The guest was satisfied with the overall service.

AYS placed an incorrect order for room 408 and the guest noticed once the order had been delivered. We apologised to the guest and immediately arranged for the correct order to be delivered. The guest was satisfied with the prompt service.
There was a food delay of 20 - 30 minutes for a serve of olives around 19:00 PM. It was taken off the cheque and the guest was satisfied.

A new entree special, Chargrilled Calamari, was introduced during the service. A total of 5 servings were sold, and the dish was well recieved by the guests, with positive feedback noted throughout the evening.
Exchange Lane remained consistently busy throughout the evening, with  a steady flow of guests and no quiet periods. Around 21:00 PM, the bar became particularly busy.

In room dining experienced  a surge in orders between 20:00 to 22:30 PM. Additionally, a $40 in room dining transaction was processed, and the corresponding cash has been deposited under the Exchange Lane PM system in the cash drop machine.

An in-house guest on table 12 dined in Penny Blue for oysters and drinks since the bar was at full capacity. The guests ordered a rum brulee to start, which experienced a delay due to a busy bar, followed by kilpatrick oysters, which were served within 15 minutes. The guest was slightly intoxicated and repeatedly requested immediate service despite being informed of the expected waiting time. Aplogies were extended, however the guest remained dissatisfied at the conclusion of service.

An incorrect order was taken by AYS for Room 1208, where a mushrrom burger was delivered instead of a Marriott burger. The error was identified after delivery, and the correct order was sent to the room shortly thereafter. The guest was satisfied overall.   Additionally, Room 614 ordered a marriott burger via AYS with no tomato sauce ,no burger sauce, no pickles and asked for lettuce and tomato to be added. However, it was not mentioned in the KOT and the guest was really unhappy with the burger. As a part of service recovery, the manager went upto the guest room and inquired about the order and offered chocolates to the guest. The burger was taken off the cheque and the guest was understanding.
We had 29 guests reserved before service and recieved alot of walk-ins between 18:45 to 20:00. We did a total of 59 guests tonight. Overall guests were happy with the food and service.
The bar was consistently busy between 17:30 and 22:00 due to the constant inflow of guests from the Ashes.

Ms. DJ from room 1402 was extremely dissapointed with the food and sent it back to the kitchen to remake multiple times. The cheque was taken care of and the guest was really satisfied with the overall service and experience. The breakfast team has been informed to HWC.

Guest from Room 1305 ordered a serve of fries and a glass of wine to their room, however, the order was delayed due to multiple orders. The guest had to wait for 50 minutes for their order to be delivered. The guest was informed and as a part of service recovery their cheque was taken care of.
The Elders Group arrived at the bar at 22:30, prompting extended service. The bar remianed open for them until 23:30.
We sold a few good bottles of wine such as La Chablisienne and Peppoli Chianti DOCG.
Exchange Lane got busy between 15:30 - 19:00, we sold a few bottles of Pol Roger Champagne, Shaw + Smith M3 Chardonnay, Atarangi Pinot Noir etc.
IRD received a surge in orders between 18:00 - 19:00 and 22:30 - 23:30. All orders were delivered in a timely manner with no delays.

Room 1124 mentioned that the food was not upto the prefered temperature. As a part of service recovery a creme brulee was offered which was declined by the guest. The guest made a persistent request for the charges to be removed, and the charges were subsequently waived.
The Master Builder group came into the bar at 10:50 pm and were there until 00:30 am. Additionally, $5500 from Exchange Lane dinner revenue belongs to BP cokctail event from 26/11/2025.

For tonights event, the group arrived at 7:50pm, an hour earlier than their scheduled time at 8:45 PM. The guests were in a rush to have food. The entrees were served on time, but the mains were slightly delayed, which led to some guests being upset. However, the desserts were served smoothly, and the guests were very happy with the food and overall experience.

Room 622 requested cutlery to be sent to their room, however, since it was busy the delivery was delayed.                                                                                                  Room 409's order docket was missed by the kitchen, hence, it was delayed by an hour. The kitchen was informed and the meal was prepared and delivered in next 15 min.

Two tables from Room 307 and Room 1104 experienced a 30 minute delay in recieving their food since the kitchen missed their dockets. The guests were unhappy, however, we offered a round of complimentary drinks to Room 304. The breakfast team has been informed to take special care of them.

Due to a fire alarm activation and the hood suppression system being triggered in the ground-level kitchen at 22:14, several orders were delayed while the fire brigade investigated the cause of the alert. All affected guests were contacted, informed of the situation, and advised of potential delays to their meals. Appropriate service recovery measures were provided, and all impacted guests were understanding once notified.

Room 405 reported multiple issues with their order. The bolognese was first returned for being cold, and when remade the guest stated they did not like the taste and noted fingerpints on the plate. The guest then ordered a club sandwich, which they reported had pink, uncooked chicken. All food items were voided, and complimentary drinks were offered, however the guest declined.
